mainTopic: Kosher hide for holy work (תחש and תפילין straps), and the dispute over a folded cloth wick
overview: The amud opens with a קל וחומר from goats' hair: even the hide of a non-kosher animal becomes טמא as a tent over a dead body, so the משכן's covering did not have to be kosher. The גמרא then searches for the purpose of רב יוסף's teaching that only kosher-animal hide was fit for heavenly work. The parchment, the boxes, and the hair and sinews of תפילין are each already covered by a פסוק or a הלכה למשה מסיני. The answer that holds is the רצועות: the tradition only says they must be black, so רב יוסף teaches they must come from a kosher animal. Next, רבי מאיר describes the תחש as a one-horned creature; its single horn shows it was kosher, but whether it was a חיה or a בהמה stays undecided. A new משנה follows: רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא disagree whether a folded, unsinged cloth wick is טמא and may be lit. The גמרא explains the lighting dispute through an exactly 3x3 cloth lit on a יום טוב that falls on ערב שבת, and רב יוסף confirms it from his tradition. The amud ends with a challenge to רב אדא בר אהבה's view, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proving non-kosher hide becomes impure as a tent over the dead
steps.stepSummary: A קל וחומר from goats' hair shows that non-kosher animal hide becomes טמא באהל המת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned through a קל וחומר from goats' hair. Goats' hair does not become impure through צרעת, yet it does become impure as a tent over a dead body. So the hide of a non-kosher animal, which does become impure through צרעת, should surely become impure as a tent over a dead body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that the hide of a non-kosher animal can become טמא as an אהל המת. It does this by comparing it to goats' hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Goats' hair is the 'weaker' item, because it is not affected by נגעים, yet it still becomes טמא באהל המת. Non-kosher hide is the 'stronger' item, because it is affected by נגעים. So it should certainly become טמא באהל המת. This sets up the next question, because now the משכן's covering did not need to be from a kosher animal.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a weaker case to a stronger case
צרעת-type affliction that can make garments and hides impure
The impurity of a tent or covering over a dead body
Is it not logical? (the closing formula of a קל וחומר)

phrases.aramaic: אָתְיָא בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר מִנּוֹצָה שֶׁל עִזִּים,
phrases.english: It comes through an a fortiori argument from goats' hair,
which does not become impure through leprosy —
phrases.notes: This is the weaker side of the comparison.

phrases.english: yet it becomes impure as a tent over the dead;
the hide of a non-kosher animal, which does become impure through leprosy —
phrases.notes: This is the stronger side of the comparison.

phrases.english: is it not logical that it becomes impure as a tent over the dead?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָתְיָא בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר מִנּוֹצָה שֶׁל עִזִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the משכן covering by establishing the impurity status of non-kosher hide.
steps.raayaObject: That non-kosher animal hide becomes טמא באהל המת

steps.title: What is רב יוסף's teaching for?
steps.stepSummary: If the משכן did not need kosher hide, what practical law does רב יוסף's teaching come to teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what about רב יוסף's teaching: 'Only the hide of a kosher animal was fit for heavenly work'? What law is that for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the purpose of רב יוסף's teaching. If it is not about the משכן, what is it about?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 showed that even non-kosher hide could be the טמא covering of the משכן. So רב יוסף cannot be talking about the משכן. The גמרא now needs to find a real application for his rule.

phrases.english: But then, that which Rav Yosef taught:
Nothing was made fit for heavenly work
except the hide of a kosher animal alone —
for what law is it relevant?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּתָנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a consequence from Step 1 that seems to leave רב יוסף's teaching without a purpose.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משכן covering need not be kosher, רב יוסף's teaching seems to have no application.

steps.title: It is about tefillin
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף's teaching applies to תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is for תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב יוסף's rule is about תפילין. תפילין must be made from a kosher animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This moves רב יוסף's rule from the משכן to another kind of 'heavenly work.' This first answer covers the תפילין in general, mainly the parchment.

phrases.english: For tefillin.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִתְפִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the rule to a different case
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יוסף's teaching applies to תפילין.

steps.title: Tefillin already have an explicit verse
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק already teaches that תפילין must come from something permitted to eat, so רב יוסף's teaching is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: תפילין? It is written about them openly: 'So that the תורה of ה׳ will be in your mouth.' This means they must be made from what is permitted in your mouth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the answer. The rule for תפילין is already written in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'בפיך' are read to mean that תפילין must come from an animal you may eat. So רב יוסף's teaching would add nothing new for תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: From what is permitted in your mouth (permitted to eat)

phrases.english: Tefillin? It is written explicitly about them:
"So that the law of the Lord may be in your mouth" (Exodus 13:9),
meaning: from what is permitted in your mouth!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּפִילִּין בְּהֶדְיָא כְּתִיב בְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רב יוסף refers to תפילין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק already teaches this, so רב יוסף's teaching would be unnecessary.

steps.title: It is about the leather of the tefillin boxes
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף's teaching refers to the leather boxes of תפילין, not the parchment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is for their leather.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the answer. The פסוק covers the parchment, and רב יוסף teaches that the leather boxes must also be from a kosher animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that 'בפיך' refers only to the parchment with words of תורה on it. So a separate teaching would be needed for the leather housing.

phrases.english: Rather, for their leather.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְעוֹרָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 4 by narrowing which part of the תפילין is meant.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יוסף's teaching applies to the leather boxes of תפילין.

steps.title: The boxes have a הלכה למשה מסיני too
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the שין on the box is a הלכה למשה מסיני. So the boxes are part of Torah law, and the kosher rule already covers them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't אביי say: the שין of the תפילין is a law given to משה at סיני!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer using אביי's statement about the שין on the box.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the box carries a הלכה למשה מסיני, then it counts as a Torah-level part of the תפילין, just like the parchment. So the kosher requirement already applies to it. רב יוסף's teaching would again add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: The raised letter שין on the head-תפילין box
An oral law given to משה at סיני

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not discussing kosher leather directly. His point is only that the box has Torah-level status. From that, the גמרא infers that the kosher rule covers the box too.

phrases.english: But didn't Abaye say:
The shin of the tefillin
is a law given to Moses at Sinai!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רב יוסף refers to the leather boxes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The boxes have Torah-level status, so the kosher requirement is already known for them.

steps.title: It is about the hair and sinews used for tefillin
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף's teaching refers to tying the תפילין with kosher-animal hair and sewing them with kosher-animal sinews.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is for tying them with their hair and sewing them with their sinews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a third answer. רב יוסף teaches that the hair used to tie the parchments and the sinews used to sew the boxes must come from a kosher animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hair and sinew are small extra parts, not the parchment or the box itself. So maybe a separate teaching is needed to require them to be kosher too.

phrases.english: Rather, to tie them with their hair
and to sew them with their sinews.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְכוֹרְכָן בְּשַׂעֲרָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 6 with a third application.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יוסף's teaching applies to the hair and sinews of תפילין.

steps.title: Hair and sinews are also a הלכה למשה מסיני
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists tying with hair and sewing with sinews as a הלכה למשה מסיני. So רב יוסף's teaching is still not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This too is a law given to משה at סיני, as a ברייתא teaches: תפילין must be square, which is a law given to משה at סיני. They are tied with their hair and sewn with their sinews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the third answer as well. A ברייתא says the hair-and-sinew rule is already a הלכה למשה מסיני. The next step drops this answer and offers a new one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the hair and sinew rule is a הלכה למשה מסיני, it is already known at Torah level. רב יוסף would not need to teach it. So the search for the purpose of his teaching goes on.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: Three uses of רב יוסף's rule were proposed: the parchment, the boxes, and the hair and sinews. Each one is already covered by a פסוק or a הלכה למשה מסיני. Steps 9-11 finally find its purpose: the רצועות.

phrases.aramaic: הָא נָמֵי הֲלָכָה לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי הוּא,
phrases.english: This too is a law given to Moses at Sinai,
as it was taught in a baraita:
Tefillin being square —
is a law given to Moses at Sinai;
they are tied with their hair
and sewn with their sinews!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא נָמֵי הֲלָכָה לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רב יוסף refers to the hair and sinews
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא already lists this as a הלכה למשה מסיני, so רב יוסף's teaching would be unnecessary.

steps.title: רב יוסף's teaching is about the straps
steps.stepSummary: After the earlier answers were knocked down, the גמרא suggests רב יוסף's teaching refers to the straps (רצועות) of תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף's teaching is about the straps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a fresh attempt to explain why רב יוסף's teaching is needed. It says the teaching is about the straps of the תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The parchment, the boxes, and the hair and sinews are all already covered by other sources. So the גמרא moves to the one part not yet discussed, the רצועות. The claim is that רב יוסף is teaching that the straps must come from a kosher animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces a new answer after the old one fell
The leather straps of the תפילין

phrases.english: Rather, it is for the straps.
phrases.notes: רב יוסף's rule is now applied to the straps of the תפילין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לִרְצוּעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the קשיא in step 8 by moving רב יוסף's teaching to a new object, the straps.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-assigning the teaching to a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יוסף's teaching was about the hair and sinews, which a ברייתא already covers.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יוסף's teaching is about the leather straps of תפילין.

steps.title: The straps already have a הלכה למשה מסיני
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק said that black straps are a הלכה למשה מסיני, so the straps also seem to be covered already.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי יצחק say that black straps are a הלכה למשה מסיני?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer. It points out that the straps are also part of a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This attack follows the same pattern as steps 6 and 8. If the straps are part of the Torah-level מצוה, the kosher rule from the פסוק should already cover them. Then רב יוסף's teaching would again add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [so-and-so] say? A formula that opens a challenge
A law given orally to משה at Sinai

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yitzchak say:
Black straps
phrases.notes: The straps of תפילין must be black.

phrases.english: are a law given to Moses at Sinai?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the תירוץ of step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב יוסף's teaching is needed for the straps
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The straps are a הלכה למשה מסיני, so they belong to the מצוה itself. The פסוק requiring kosher material should already include them, which makes רב יוסף's teaching unnecessary.

steps.title: The tradition said black, not kosher
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה למשה מסיני only taught that the straps must be black. It never taught that they must be from a kosher animal, so רב יוסף is needed for that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, we learned by tradition that they must be black. Did we learn that they must be from a kosher animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the answer. The הלכה למשה מסיני about the straps only covers their color.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the boxes and the hair and sinews, the הלכה למשה מסיני made them part of the מצוה itself. With the straps, the tradition only set one detail, the color black. It said nothing about where the leather must come from. So רב יוסף's teaching is what tells us the straps must be from a kosher animal.
steps.whatToRemember: The final answer is that רב יוסף's teaching (only kosher-animal material for holy work) applies to the רצועות of תפילין. The הלכה למשה מסיני only required them to be black.

phrases.english: Granted that we learned by tradition that they are black,
did we learn by tradition that they are kosher?
phrases.notes: No. So רב יוסף's teaching is needed for this.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְהִי דִּגְמִירִי שְׁחוֹרוֹת, טְהוֹרוֹת מִי גְּמִירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10 and closes the discussion of רב יוסף's teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the other source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The הלכה למשה מסיני about straps makes them fully part of the מצוה, so the kosher rule already covers them.
steps.terutzMaskana: The tradition only set the color. The kosher requirement for straps comes from רב יוסף.

steps.title: What was decided about the תחש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the earlier question of what the תחש from משה's time was.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the conclusion about the תחש that existed in the days of משה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the bigger question it raised earlier on the דף. It asks for a final answer about the תחש. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The talk about רב יוסף and תפילין started as a side path from the question of whether the תחש was kosher. Now the גמרא asks directly for the final ruling about this animal.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the conclusion about it?
The animal whose skin was used to cover the משכן

phrases.english: What is the conclusion about
the tachash that existed in the days of Moses?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הָוֵי עֲלֵהּ דְּתַחַשׁ שֶׁהָיָה בִּימֵי מֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תפילין discussion and returns to the earlier question about the תחש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of animal was the תחש, and was it kosher?

steps.title: רבי מאיר describes the one-horned תחש
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר teaches that the תחש was a creature of its own kind. The חכמים could not decide whether it was a חיה or a בהמה. It had one horn on its forehead, came to משה only for building the משכן, and then disappeared.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעא said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש that רבי מאיר used to say: the תחש of משה's time was a creature of its own kind. The חכמים did not decide whether it was a wild animal or a domestic animal. It had one horn on its forehead. It appeared to משה just for that time, he made the משכן covering from it, and then it was hidden away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with רבי מאיר's description of the תחש. He calls it a one-of-a-kind, one-horned animal that appeared only for the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer gives two key facts: the חיה-or-בהמה question was left open, and the animal had a single horn. The single horn becomes the clue the גמרא uses in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A creature of its own kind
It was hidden away; it disappeared

steps.confusionAlert: Two separate questions are in play: (1) was the תחש kosher, and (2) was it a חיה or a בהמה? רבי מאיר only says the second question was left undecided.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ela said
that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said,
Rabbi Meir used to say:
The tachash that existed in the days of Moses
was a creature of its own kind,
and the Sages did not decide about it

phrases.aramaic: אִם מִין חַיָּה הוּא, אִם מִין בְּהֵמָה הוּא.
phrases.english: whether it is a type of wild animal or a type of domestic animal.
And it had one horn on its forehead,
and it came to Moses just for that time,
and he made the Tabernacle covering from it, and it was hidden away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִלָּעָא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ, אוֹמֵר הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תחש was a unique one-horned creature. Whether it was a חיה or a בהמה was left undecided.

steps.title: The single horn proves the תחש was kosher
steps.stepSummary: Because the תחש had one horn, it must have been kosher. רב יהודה teaches that the ox offered by אדם הראשון had one horn, based on a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it says the תחש had one horn on its forehead, we learn that it was kosher. רב יהודה said that the ox אדם הראשון offered had one horn on its forehead, as it says: 'It will please ה׳ more than an ox, a bull with horns and hooves.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from רבי מאיר's words: a one-horned animal is kosher. It brings proof from the one-horned ox of אדם הראשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal offered as a קרבן must be kosher. אדם הראשון's ox was a קרבן and had one horn, so a one-horned body type is found in a kosher animal. The single horn of the תחש therefore points to a kosher animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; we can conclude

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּקָאָמַר קֶרֶן אַחַת הָיְתָה לוֹ בְּמִצְחוֹ,
phrases.english: Since it says it had one horn on its forehead,
learn from this that it was kosher,
as Rav Yehuda said:
The ox that Adam, the first man, offered
had one horn on its forehead,
as it is said: 'And it will please the Lord more than an ox,
a bull with horns and hooves.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָאָמַר קֶרֶן אַחַת הָיְתָה לוֹ בְּמִצְחוֹ, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a halachic conclusion (kosher) from a detail in רבי מאיר's description.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה: אדם הראשון's ox, which was a קרבן, had one horn (תהלים 69:32)

steps.title: The word מקרין sounds like two horns
steps.stepSummary: The word מקרין suggests more than one horn, so the פסוק does not seem to show the ox had a single horn.
steps.simpleTranslation: But 'מקרין' means two horns!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's reading of the פסוק. The word sounds plural.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the word means two horns, the ox was a normal two-horned animal. Then the proof that one-horned animals are kosher falls apart.

phrases.english: 'Makrin' implies two!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַקְרִין תַּרְתֵּי מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading of the פסוק used as proof in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's reading of the word מקרין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word as it is read sounds plural, which points to two horns rather than one.

steps.title: The word is spelled as one horn
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the word is written without a יוד, as מקרן, which shows a single horn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: it is written 'מקרן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the spelling of the word shows one horn, even though it is read like a plural.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is read מקרין but spelled מקרן, without a יוד. The spelling hints at one horn. So רב יהודה's proof stands, and so does the conclusion that the תחש was kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written (how the word is spelled)

steps.confusionAlert: How a word is spelled (כתיב) and how it is read can differ. The דרשה here relies on the spelling, not the reading.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It is written 'makren' (without a yod).
phrases.notes: The missing יוד hints at a single horn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מַקְרָן כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15.
steps.terutzMaskana: The spelling מקרן shows one horn, so the proof stands.

steps.title: Can we also prove the תחש was a בהמה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we don't also prove that the תחש was a בהמה, since the one-horned ox was a domestic animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let us also resolve from this that it was a type of domestic animal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the same proof further. If the one horn links the תחש to an ox, that might also settle that it was a בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ox is a בהמה. If the one-horn feature compares the תחש to the ox for being kosher, it should also compare them for being a בהמה. That would settle the question רבי מאיר said the חכמים left open.

phrases.english: So let us resolve from it
that it is a type of domestic animal?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיפְשׁוֹט מִינֵּיהּ דְּמִין בְּהֵמָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the proof from steps 14 and 16 to try to settle the open question from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's statement that the חכמים did not decide between חיה and בהמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the one-horned ox proves the תחש was kosher, the same comparison should prove it was a בהמה, so the question should not have been left open.

steps.title: The קרש shows a one-horned wild animal
steps.stepSummary: The קרש is a חיה with only one horn. So a single horn does not prove an animal is a בהמה, and the question stays open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since there is the קרש, which is a wild animal and has only one horn, one could say the תחש was a wild animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the attempt to prove the תחש was a בהמה. A one-horned חיה also exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One horn is found in both kinds of animals: the ox (a בהמה) and the קרש (a חיה). So one horn can show the animal was kosher, but it cannot show which kind it was. רבי מאיר's statement stands: the חיה-or-בהמה question stays unresolved.
steps.whatToRemember: Final picture of the תחש: it was kosher (proved by its single horn), but whether it was a חיה or a בהמה is left unresolved.

phrases.english: Since there is the keresh,
which is a type of wild animal,
and it has only one horn,
one can say that it is a type of wild animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא קֶרֶשׁ דְּמִין חַיָּה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by showing the proof cannot settle the חיה-or-בהמה question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One horn links the תחש to the ox, so it must be a בהמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The one-horned קרש is a חיה, so one horn only proves the animal was kosher, not which kind it was.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The תחש was kosher. Whether it was a חיה or a בהמה remains undecided.

steps.title: A folded cloth wick that was not singed
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a piece of cloth was folded into a wick but not yet singed. רבי אליעזר says it can still become טמא and may not be lit on שבת. רבי עקיבא says it is טהור and may be lit.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A wick made from a garment that was folded but not singed: רבי אליעזר says it is טמא and one may not light with it. רבי עקיבא says it is טהור and one may light with it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא argue about whether a folded cloth wick still counts as a garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether folding the cloth is enough to turn it from a garment into a wick. רבי אליעזר holds it is still a garment: it can become טמא and is not fit for lighting on שבת. רבי עקיבא holds folding already made it a wick: it is no longer a garment that can become טמא, and it may be lit.

keyTerms.meaning: He singed it (burned it lightly to make lighting easier)
Able to become ritually impure / ritually pure

steps.whyThisMatters: The argument hinges on when an object changes its legal identity, from garment to wick. That change affects both טומאה and the laws of שבת lighting.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A wick made from a garment
that one folded but did not singe,
Rabbi Eliezer says: It is ritually impure,
and one may not light with it.
Rabbi Akiva says: It is ritually pure,
and one may light with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ פְּתִילַת הַבֶּגֶד שֶׁקִּיפְּלָהּ וְלֹא הִבְהֲבָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic, unrelated to the תחש discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: a folded, unsinged cloth wick is still טמא and may not be lit. רבי עקיבא: it is טהור and may be lit.

steps.title: The impurity side of the dispute is easy to explain
steps.stepSummary: On טומאה, רבי אליעזר holds folding does not change the cloth, so it stays a garment. רבי עקיבא holds folding cancels its garment status.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Granted, about impurity, this is what they argue about. רבי אליעזר holds that folding does nothing, and the cloth stays in its first status. רבי עקיבא holds that folding works, and it cancels the cloth's garment status.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by explaining the part of the משנה that is easy: why they argue about טומאה. This is a setup line. It prepares the real question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole argument is whether folding a cloth into a wick shape takes away its identity as a garment. If folding does nothing, the cloth is still a garment and can become טמא. If folding works, the cloth is now just a wick and is טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / this part is fine (sets up a 'but' question)
Folding (twisting the cloth into a wick)

steps.confusionAlert: בשלמא does not end the discussion. It means 'this part is fine, BUT...' A harder question is always coming right after it.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Granted, regarding impurity,
in this they disagree:

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר קִיפּוּל אֵינוֹ מוֹעִיל
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds that folding is not effective,
and it remains in its original status.
And Rabbi Akiva holds that folding is effective,
and he has nullified its (garment) status.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְעִנְיַן טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's analysis of the משנה quoted in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The טומאה dispute is about whether folding cancels a cloth's garment status.

steps.title: But why argue about lighting it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the lighting dispute could depend on.
steps.simpleTranslation: But about lighting, what do they argue about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the real question. Why should it matter for lighting on שבת whether the cloth is still a garment?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether a cloth can become טמא seems to have nothing to do with whether it may be lit. So the גמרא needs a case where the garment status of the cloth also controls the lighting.

phrases.english: But regarding lighting, about what do they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְעִנְיַן הַדְלָקָה בְּמַאי פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא...אלא structure begun in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the lighting part of the dispute depends on.

steps.title: The case: an exact 3x3 cloth on a יום טוב before שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר in the name of רב אושעיא, and also רב אדא בר אהבה, set the case. The cloth is exactly 3x3 fingerbreadths, and the day is a יום טוב that falls on ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רב אושעיא, and רב אדא בר אהבה said the same: here we are dealing with a cloth that is exactly three by three. And we are dealing with a יום טוב that falls on ערב שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by describing a very specific case. The next steps explain why each detail matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 3x3 fingerbreadths is the smallest size of cloth that counts as a garment. If the cloth is exactly that size, burning even a little makes it too small to count. Setting the case on יום טוב means the lighting itself is happening on a holy day, so the rules of what may be burned on יום טוב apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Three by three fingerbreadths: the minimum size of a garment
Exactly / precisely, not a bit more

steps.confusionAlert: The lighting here is not on שבת itself. It is the שבת lamp being lit on Friday, which happens to be יום טוב.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said that Rav Oshaya said,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: and Rav Adda bar Ahava said likewise:

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא בְּשָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ מְצוּמְצָמוֹת עָסְקִינַן,
phrases.english: Here we are dealing with exactly three by three,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְיוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת עָסְקִינַן.
phrases.english: and we are dealing with a Festival that fell on Shabbat eve.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּשָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ מְצוּמְצָמוֹת עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 by narrowing the case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is about an exact 3x3 cloth lit on a יום טוב that falls on ערב שבת.

steps.title: Two rules both sides agree on
steps.stepSummary: Both sides accept רבי יהודה's rule that broken vessels may not be burned on יום טוב. They also accept עולא's rule that one must light most of the part of the wick that sticks out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone holds like רבי יהודה, who said: on יום טוב we may use vessels as fuel, but we may not use broken pieces of vessels as fuel. And everyone holds like עולא, who said: one who lights must light most of the part that sticks out.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer continues by listing two rules that both רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא accept. The next step uses these rules to explain their dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vessel that breaks on יום טוב counts as something 'newly made' that day, so it is מוקצה and may not be burned. עולא's rule means the lighter must burn a large part of the wick, not just its tip. Together, these mean the lighter will certainly turn the cloth into a 'broken vessel' while he is lighting it.

keyTerms.meaning: Most of the part of the wick that sticks out

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: For everyone holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
who said: one may kindle with vessels,
but one may not kindle with broken vessels.
And everyone holds like Ulla,
for Ulla said:
One who lights must light most of the part that protrudes.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the shared rules that make the case in step 22 work.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both sides accept that broken vessels may not be burned on יום טוב, and that one must light most of the protruding wick.

steps.title: Applying the rules to each side
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר: the cloth is still a vessel, so lighting it makes it a broken vessel, which is forbidden. רבי עקיבא: it is no longer a vessel at all, so it is just like burning wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר holds that folding does nothing. So once he lights a little of it, it becomes a broken vessel, and when he goes on lighting, he is lighting a broken vessel. רבי עקיבא holds that folding works, and it no longer has the status of a vessel. So when he lights it, he is just lighting plain wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by showing how each side reaches its ruling about lighting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, the cloth is still a garment. As soon as a little burns, it drops below 3x3 and becomes a 'broken vessel.' Since he must keep lighting most of the wick, he ends up burning a broken vessel, which is forbidden. For רבי עקיבא, the folding already took away its vessel status before יום טוב, so nothing 'breaks' on יום טוב and lighting is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: The lighting dispute is the same as the טומאה dispute. Does folding cancel the cloth's garment status? If not, burning it on יום טוב means burning a 'broken vessel.'

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר קִיפּוּל אֵינוֹ מוֹעִיל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds that folding is not effective,
and once he lights a little of it,
it becomes a broken vessel,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי קָא מַדְלֵיק — בְּשֶׁבֶר כְּלִי קָמַדְלֵיק.
phrases.english: and when he lights, he is lighting with a broken vessel.
And Rabbi Akiva holds that folding is effective,
and it does not have the status of a vessel,
and when he lights, he is lighting with mere wood.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר קִיפּוּל אֵינוֹ מוֹעִיל, וְכֵיוָן דְּאַדְלֵיק בֵּיהּ פּוּרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the shared rules from step 23 to each side of the dispute.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The lighting dispute depends on whether folding removes the cloth's vessel status, given the יום טוב ban on burning broken vessels.

steps.title: רב יוסף finally understands a teaching he had
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף had learned 'exactly three by three' without knowing why it mattered. Now he sees it explains this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: this is what we learned, 'exactly three by three,' and I did not know what law it was for.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף backs up the answer just given. He had a tradition about 'exactly 3x3' that now makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's teachers taught this case with the detail 'exactly 3x3,' but he did not know why that detail was needed. The answer above shows the reason: only an exact 3x3 cloth becomes a 'broken vessel' as soon as a little of it burns. So his tradition supports the explanation.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: this is what we learned:
"Exactly three by three,"
and I did not know for what law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, הַיְינוּ דְּתָנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the case set up in step 22 with a received tradition.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה deals with an exactly 3x3 cloth.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יוסף's tradition: 'שלש על שלש מצומצמות.'

steps.title: So רב אדא בר אהבה holds like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Because רב אדא בר אהבה explained the משנה using רבי יהודה's rule, the גמרא concludes that he himself holds like רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since רב אדא בר אהבה explained the משנה according to רבי יהודה, we learn from this that he holds like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a side point about רב אדא בר אהבה's own opinion. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a sage explains a משנה in a way that fits his own view. So the גמרא assumes רב אדא בר אהבה agrees with רבי יהודה that broken vessels may not be burned on יום טוב, which means he accepts the idea of מוקצה from things newly made on יום טוב.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִדְּקָא מְתָרֵץ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
phrases.english: And from the fact that Rav Adda bar Ahava explains
according to Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: learn from this that he holds like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּקָא מְתָרֵץ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a side conclusion from רב אדא בר אהבה's role in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אדא בר אהבה holds like רבי יהודה about broken vessels on יום טוב.

steps.title: Did רב אדא בר אהבה really say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the inference by bringing up another statement of רב אדא בר אהבה. That statement is quoted in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: But did רב אדא בר אהבה really say this? Didn't רב אדא בר אהבה say:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge against step 26. It is about to quote a different statement of רב אדא בר אהבה that seems to go against רבי יהודה. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge says that רב אדא בר אהבה's own words elsewhere seem to contradict the claim that he holds like רבי יהודה. Only the opening formula appears here. The actual contradicting statement comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? (introduces a contradiction)

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה הָכִי?
phrases.english: But did Rav Adda bar Ahava say this?
But didn't Rav Adda bar Ahava say:

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב אדא בר אהבה holds like רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another statement of his (quoted next) seems to contradict holding like רבי יהודה.
